subject: OrderForm SLA — maintenance blackout carveouts & response tiers
messages:

Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: OrderForm SLA: maintenance blackout carveouts & response tiers

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement is reviewing the draft order form and has two items they want clarified before we sign:

1) Maintenance blackout carveouts — Vasta runs quarterly scheduled platform upgrades and has two windows (one 2-hour weekly patch window and one quarterly 4-hour major window). They want to confirm how those windows are treated against the uptime SLA and whether we can designate them as "blackout carveouts" that don't count toward availability calculations.

2) Response tiers & credits — They want explicit response/resolution targets for P1/P2/P3 and a simple service credit formula (we prefer percentage of monthly fees per minute/hour of downtime). They also asked about caps on aggregate credits and whether emergency security patches would be excluded from credit triggers.

I've attached the procurement team's redline notes for context. Can we get a short, concrete counterproposal that we can take back to them (they're hoping to close this week)?

Best,
Tom
Tom Hayes
Director, IT Procurement
Vasta Health
Attachments: Vasta_SLA_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrderForm SLA: maintenance blackout carveouts & response tiers

Tom —

Thanks for sending this over. We're aligned on wanting simple, measurable language so there's no ambiguity at renewal. Quick counterproposal below (summarized) — happy to put into redline form and join procurement for a quick call:

- Availability target: 99.95% measured as total successful request count over total attempted requests per calendar month (we can also use rolling 30-day; legal preference?).
- Planned maintenance: Redwood will provide >=72 hours notice for planned maintenance >=30 minutes. Planned maintenance is excluded from SLA calculations if advanced notice is provided and the maintenance is scheduled within a 4-hour window.
- Emergency/patch exceptions: Security patches that must be applied immediately to mitigate an active exploit will be excluded from credits provided we notify Vasta within 4 hours of the change and provide a post-mortem within 72 hours.
- Response tiers (acknowledge / initial response): P1 (service down): 15 minutes, P2 (severe degradation): 60 minutes, P3 (minor): 4 hours. Resolution targets vary by issue type; we'll map on call.
- Credits: 5% of monthly invoice for each cumulative 30 minutes of downtime beyond the availability target, capped at 25% of the monthly invoice. Credits apply only to the product charges on the order form (not to third-party pass-through costs).

Action items I propose:
1) Kimberly/legal to prepare redlined language for the Order Form + MSA scope (I can draft technical appendix).
2) Quick call — 30 minutes today or tomorrow to finalize.

I've attached a draft redline we can circulate (Vasta_SLA_Redline_20280410.pdf).

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Vasta_SLA_Redline_20280410.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrderForm SLA: maintenance blackout carveouts & response tiers

Mateo —

Reviewing Tom's procurement notes and your summary. A few legal redline suggestions (high level) before we send to Vasta:

1) Measurement window: prefer "availability measured over a rolling 30-day window" to avoid calendar-month edge cases. This also aligns with our instrumentation granularity.

2) Credit formula: prefer to express credits as "(Monthly Service Fee) * (credit % per minute)" where credit % per minute = 0.0001157407 (equivalent to 5% for each 30-minute bucket) — but also propose simplifying language: "5% of Monthly Service Fee per 30-minute downtime bucket, prorated to the nearest minute."

3) Aggregate cap: legal recommends a hard cap at 25% of the Monthly Service Fee per billing period, but add carveout for bona fide force majeure events (list to be mutually agreed).

4) Planned maintenance notice: change 72 hours to ">=72 hours notice for maintenance windows >60 minutes" and require a maintenance report within 48 hours of completion for windows >2 hours.

5) Emergency patch carveout: retain but require customer acknowledgement (email) within 48 hours, not 4, to make operationally reasonable. If we accept Vasta's 4-hour notice requirement, ops will need a formal SLA with on-call shift coverage and runbook.

6) Escalation path: include a 3-tier escalation contact list (primary on-call, backup on-call, Director-level on-call) with 24x7 phone numbers and an SSO-protected incident page. We can redact direct numbers in the order form and place them in an Ops Appendix.

I'm attaching a cleaned matrix of proposed wording (Redline_Matrix_Cleaned.xlsx). I recommend we (a) accept the rolling 30-day measurement; (b) keep 5%/30min buckets; (c) add the 25% cap and force majeure carveout; and (d) negotiate Vasta's request to mark quarterly windows as "blackout carveouts" to instead allow a set of "pre-approved maintenance windows" listed in the Ops Appendix.

If you want, legal can send a marked-up Order Form and MSA excerpt for Vasta to review.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redline_Matrix_Cleaned.xlsx

Thanks for the quick turnaround — and thanks Kim for the redlines. A couple of asks from procurement/legal on our side:

- One emergency window allowance: Can we agree to one 2-hour emergency maintenance event per calendar quarter that is treated as an exception (no credit) if Redwood provides notice within 4 hours and the event impacts <0.1% of total requests for that period? This helps our security team when we need to perform non-scheduled critical updates.

- Escalation contacts: please provide the primary on-call phone and backup contact. Procurement will accept a redacted phone in the Order Form if the Ops Appendix includes full numbers and escalation SLAs.

If you can accept the above and send the marked-up Order Form, procurement will review and aim to finalize by EOD Friday.

On the call point — we're available Thu 11:00–13:00 PT or Fri 09:00–11:00 PT.

Regards,
Tom Hayes

Vasta Health

Tom —

Appreciate the clarity. We can accept one 2-hour emergency exception per calendar quarter under the conditions you specified (notify within 4 hours and impact <0.1% of total requests). We'll capture that as a narrowly worded carveout in the Ops Appendix rather than the main SLA to avoid broad precedent.

Escalation contacts: we'll include a 3-tier contact list in the Ops Appendix (primary on-call, backup on-call, Director on-call). We'll redact phone numbers in the Order Form and place them in the Appendix, which will be attached to the Order Form and referenced by DocuSign.
